q: 1. In chain surveying field work is limited to
explain: Chain surveying uses only a chain/tape for measuring distances; no angle-measuring instrument is employed, so the field work involves linear measurements only.

q: 2. Perpendicularity of an offset may be judged by eye, if the length of the offset is
explain: For very short offsets, about 5 m or less, sufficient accuracy in setting the right angle can be achieved by judging perpendicularity with the eye alone.

q: 3. When the length of chain used in measuring distance is longer than the standard length, the error in measured distance will be ...............
explain: If the chain is too long, it measures a shorter distance than actual, resulting in a negative error (Correction is positive).

q: 4. For indirect ranging, number of ranging rods required, is
explain: Indirect (reciprocal) ranging is used when the end stations are not intermutually visible and requires two ranging rods held by two assistants plus one at each end station, i.e., four rods in total.

q: 5. Greater accuracy in linear measurements, is obtained by ...............
explain: Invar tapes have a very low coefficient of thermal expansion, making them the most accurate for baseline measurements.

q: 6. It is more difficult to obtain good results while measuring horizontal distance by stepping ...............
explain: Stepping uphill is harder because the person at the front must maintain alignment and plumbing while looking 'up' the slope.

q: 7. Cross staff is an instrument used for ...............
explain: A cross-staff is a simple instrument used in chain surveying to set out perpendicular offsets (right angles) from the chain line.

q: 8. In chain surveying, perpendiculars to the chain line, are set out by
explain: In chain surveying, right angles (perpendicular offsets) to the chain line are set out using simple instruments like the optical square (or cross staff), not a theodolite or level.

q: 9. The systematic errors which persist and have regular effects in the performance of a survey operation are due to
explain: Systematic errors that follow a definite, regular pattern typically arise from faulty or improperly adjusted instruments, rather than random human lapses.

q: 10. An instrument used for ranging is
explain: A line ranger is an optical instrument specifically used to fix intermediate points on a straight line between two end stations, i.e., for ranging.

q: 11. The angle of intersection of the horizon glass and index glass in an optical square is ...............
explain: The two mirrors of an optical square are fixed at an angle of 45° to reflect rays through 90°.

q: 12. The accuracy of measurement in chain surveying does not depend upon:
options: general layout of the chain lines
explain: D) **general layout of the chain lines**: While the layout affects the efficiency of the survey, the technical accuracy of an individual measurement depends on the length of the offset, the scale used for plotting, and the precision required for the specific feature.

q: 13. Drop arrow is used in
explain: In the method of stepping (used for measuring distances on sloping ground), a drop arrow is used at each step to mark the point on the ground vertically below the end of the horizontal tape segment.

q: 14. The instrument, belonging to a class of reflecting instrument is ...............
explain: All these instruments use the principles of reflection (mirrors or prisms) to align sights or read scales.

q: 15. When the object lies on the left hand side of the chain line, then while taking offset with an optical square, it is held in ...............
explain: To view an object on the left through the reflection while staying on the line, holding it upright in the right hand is the standard procedure.

q: 16. Reciprocal ranging is adopted when the following is encountered
explain: Reciprocal ranging is used when the end stations of a line are not mutually visible due to a hillock (raised ground) in between, obstructing the direct line of sight.

q: 17. An instrument that can be used as an optical square is
explain: A box sextant is a compact instrument used for measuring horizontal and vertical angles. It can be used to set out right angles, making it a versatile alternative to the optical square.

q: 18. Reciprocal ranging is adopted when the following is encountered
explain: Reciprocal ranging (or indirect ranging) is used when the two end stations are not intervisible due to rising ground or a hillock.

q: 19. A 30 m chain after measuring a distance of 6000 m was found to be 10 cm more than the designated length. If the chain was standardized before the commencement of survey then the true length is
explain: Average error = (0 + 10)/2 = 5 cm. True distance = Measured distance * (Actual length / Design length). $6000 * (30.05 / 30) = 6010$ m.

q: 20. The walk step of a man is considered equal to:
explain: For the purpose of measuring distance by pacing, an average man's walking step (pace length) is conventionally taken as about 80 cm.

q: 21. The error in measured length due to bad ranging is
options: sometimes compensating error and sometimes cumulative error
explain: Bad ranging always makes the measured line longer than the true straight distance (a zig-zag path is longer than a straight one), so the error is always in the same (positive) direction, making it cumulative.

q: 22. The length of a link of Gunter's chain is
explain: A Gunter's chain is 66 feet long with 100 links. Each link is $66/100 = 0.66$ feet long.

q: 23. Which of the following angles can be set out with the help of French cross staff?
explain: The French cross staff has octagonal sides with slits at 45° intervals, allowing for angles of 45° and 90°.

q: 24. The permissible error in chaining for measurement with chain on rough or hilly ground is
explain: On rough or hilly ground, higher error margins are allowed; typically 1 in 250.

q: 25. The position of point can be fixed more accurately by
explain: Fixing a point by oblique offsets (measuring two distances from different known points to the same detail point) generally gives a more accurate check/fix on its position than a single perpendicular offset.

q: 26. The angle between the reflecting surface of a prism square is
explain: Like the optical square, the prism square utilizes reflecting surfaces fixed at 45° to provide a 90° deviation of light.

q: 27. Correction for slope is
explain: The approximate slope correction for a height difference 'h' over a length 'l' is $h^2 / 2l$. This is always subtractive from the measured slope distance.

q: 28. In case of a direct vernier scale
options: smallest division is longer than smallest division of the main scale
graduations increase in the same direction
explain: In a direct vernier, the scale graduations increase in the same direction as the main scale, and $n$ vernier divisions equal $(n-1)$ main scale divisions.

q: 29. Chain survey method is most suitable
options: in fairly level and open area
for large scale plans required for industrial site
explain: Chain surveying is limited to small, open, and level areas where the area can be easily divided into a network of triangles.

q: 30. The principle of chain surveying is to divided the area into a number of
explain: Triangulation is the fundamental principle of chain surveying; a triangle is the only simple plane figure that can be plotted uniquely by measuring its sides only.

q: 31. For locating the locations of the individual points according to situation we resort to
explain: Offsets (both perpendicular and oblique) are used to locate the positions of objects relative to the main survey lines.

q: 32. Direct ranging is possible only when the end stations are
options: located at highest points in the sea
explain: Direct ranging (fixing intermediate points on a line by eye alone) is possible only when the two end stations of the line are mutually intervisible.

q: 33. The tension, at which the effects of pull and sag for a tape are neutralised, is known as .............
explain: Normal tension is the specific pull applied to a tape so that the increase in length due to pull equals the decrease in length due to sag.

q: 34. The main difference between an optical square and prism square is .............
options: that optical square is more accurate than prism square
that no adjustment is required in a prism square since the angle between the reflecting surfaces cannot be changed
explain: While both use the principle of double reflection, the prism square is fixed and requires no adjustment compared to the mirrors in an optical square.

q: 35. A metallic tape is made of .............
explain: Metallic tapes are made of waterproof linen reinforced with fine brass or copper wires to prevent stretching.

q: 36. If L is the specified length of a tape, L1 its actual length and S the measured distance, then the true distance is given by the formula .............
explain: True Distance = (Actual Length / Nominal Length) x Measured Distance. If the tape is longer than specified, the recorded distance is too short, and vice versa.

q: 37. A check line in a chain surveying .............
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the surveyor to locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixed up the directions of all other lines
explain: The sole purpose of a check line (proof line) is to verify the accuracy of the framework measurements during plotting.

q: 38. The instrument used for setting out an offset at a right angle, is called .............
explain: While cross-staffs can do this, the optical square is the specific high-accuracy choice among these options for 90-degree offsets.

q: 39. For the Abney clinometer the semi-circular arc is graduated as
explain: The Abney clinometer's arc is graduated from 0° at the center to 90° on either side to measure both angles of elevation and depression.

q: 40. To use the Abney clinometer as Abney level the vernier should read
options: it is not possible to use clinometer as hand level
explain: When the vernier is set to 0°, the line of sight becomes horizontal, allowing the clinometer to function as a basic hand level.

q: 41. A scale which has a common representative fraction, but read in different measures, is called a
explain: Comparative scales (or corresponding scales) have the same R.F. but graduate in different units, like miles and kilometers.

q: 42. In a direct vernier, the smallest division of a vernier is ............ the smallest division of its primary scale.
explain: In a direct vernier, $(n-1)$ divisions of the main scale are divided into $n$ divisions on the vernier, making each vernier division slightly shorter than a main scale division.

q: 43. Measurements taken with a wrong scale can be corrected by using the relation
options: true length = (correct scale / wrong scale) × measured length
true length = (correct scale / wrong scale)² × measured length
true length = (correct scale / wrong scale)³ × measured length
explain: Linear correction is proportional to the ratio of the scales. For area, the ratio would be squared; for volume, cubed.

q: 44. The distance between steps for measuring downhill to obtain better accuracy
options: decreases with decrease of weight of the chain
explain: In the 'stepping method' of chaining on sloping ground, steps must be shorter as the slope gets steeper to maintain a horizontal chain and minimize errors.

q: 45. The position of point can be fixed more accurately by .............
explain: Perpendicular offsets are generally more accurate and easier to plot than oblique offsets because they provide the shortest distance from the chain line to the object.

q: 46. Ranging in chain survey means .............
options: establishing an intermediate point on the line
determining the distance between end points
explain: Ranging is the process of locating intermediate points on a straight line between two fixed stations so that the distance can be measured accurately.

q: 47. If the length of a chain line along a slope of θ° is l, the required slope correction is .............
explain: The correction is $l(1 - \cos \theta)$, which simplifies using trigonometric identity $1 - \cos \theta = 2 \sin^2 (\theta/2)$.

q: 48. A tape of length l and weight W kg/m is suspended at its ends with a pull of p kg, the sag correction is .............
explain: The standard formula for sag correction is $C_s =  rac{W^2 L}{24 P^2}$, where $W$ is the total weight ($w 	imes L$). If $W$ is weight per unit length, the formula is $ rac{w^2 L^3}{24 P^2}$.

q: 49. If L is the distance between two supports from which a tape is suspended under a pull P. If W is the total weight of the tape the sag correction is .............
explain: The standard formula for sag correction when using the total weight W is $C_s =  rac{W^2 L}{24 P^2}$.

q: 50. The angle between two plane mirrors of the optical square is kept .............
explain: To deflect a line of sight by 90° using reflection, the mirrors must be placed at exactly half that angle, which is 45°.
